newsitem.title: FRANCE: Cr Lyonnais head threatens to quit.
newsitem.headline: Cr Lyonnais head threatens to quit.

text.p: The chairman of state-owned Credit Lyonnais has written to the government threatening to resign unless agreement is reached by Friday on a new rescue plan for the ailing French bank, the business newspaper Les Echos reported on Thursday.
The newspaper said that a consensus "appeared to be developing" in government circles to agree to Jean Peyrelevade's demands.
But it said that the European Commission could lay down new conditions for its approval or demand a commitment by the government to speed up privatisation of the bank.
The bank, which is due to announce its half year results later this month, accumulated losses of 21 billion francs between 1992 and 1994 as a result of a reckless expansion spree.
It squeaked back into the black in 1995 with a 13 million franc profit, helped by last year's state rescue package -- the second in two years.
That plan involved spinning some 135 billion francs of its troubled assets off to a separate state holding company.

But the conditions of the state rescue package threaten to plunge it back into the red. Analysts say that unless the terms are lightened, the bank could post a full year loss of up to two billion francs this year.
